title: All-Inclusive Holidays in Rabac, Croatia 2027: Prices
metaDescription: Rabac has real all-inclusive resorts. Compare 2027 prices per person with half-board and apartments, and see who each option suits.
content:
## Does Rabac Have All-Inclusive Hotels?

Yes. Rabac, on the east coast of Istria below Labin, has a real all-inclusive offer. Valamar is the main operator. Its Rabac page lists all-inclusive resorts next to the beaches. The all-inclusive options are:

- **Valamar Bellevue Resort** (4★). It sells all-inclusive and has the plan in its name. It stands about 100 m from the beach and just over 800 m from central Rabac. The pool complex and kids' club are the main draw.
- **Girandella Family Hotel and Girandella Maro Suites & Villas**. Both are part of Girandella Resort and are marketed as family all-inclusive hotels. The Marblu show-cooking buffet is part of the package.
- **Sunny Rabac by Valamar** (3★, 180 rooms). It sells a full-board plan with meals in the Sunny restaurant, and it is often listed as an all-inclusive resort. Check the exact meal plan when booking, because it is not the same as the full all-inclusive at Bellevue.

Girandella Designed for Adults and Valamar Sanfior Hotel & Casa are sold on half board. Boutique and independent hotels such as Boutique Hotel Adoral, and the Maslinica hotels (Narcis, Hedera, Mimosa), are mostly breakfast or half-board options. Plans change from season to season, so confirm the board type before paying.

No nearby town is needed. Rabac itself is the nearest place with all-inclusive. Labin sits 4 km uphill and has no resort-style all-inclusive hotels of its own.

## What Is Typically Included

All-inclusive at Valamar resorts generally covers:

- Breakfast, lunch and dinner at a buffet or show-cooking restaurant.
- Snacks and ice cream at set hours.
- Local beer, wine and soft drinks, usually served until late evening. Guests report that cocktails and liqueurs are also included at Bellevue.
- Pool access, with sun loungers and umbrellas at the pools.
- Kids' club, animation and children's menus.

Usually **not** included: premium spirits, imported drinks, spa treatments, beach loungers outside the pool area, motorised water sports, parking at some properties, and the tourist tax. Always check the hours for drinks and snacks. Late-night drinking is not what the package is built for.

## Price per Person per Night: Peak vs Shoulder Season

The figures below are rough estimates for 2027 based on current room rates. They assume two adults sharing a standard room. Prices vary by date and by how early you book.

| Option | Peak (July–August) | Shoulder (May–June, September) |
|---|---|---|
| All-inclusive (Bellevue) | €90–130 | €55–80 |
| All-inclusive (Girandella family hotels) | €110–170 | €70–110 |
| Full board (Sunny Rabac) | €75–110 | €50–70 |
| Half-board hotel | €70–110 | €45–70 |
| Apartment, room only | €25–45 | €15–25 |
| Apartment plus own food and drink | €50–80 | €35–55 |

Current Valamar listings show Sunny Rabac from about €212 per room per night with full board, and the Sanfior and Casa on half board with soft drinks from about €102 per room in the cheapest dates. Peak weeks cost much more. Children usually get large discounts or stay free when sharing a room with two adults, which changes the maths for families.

## All-Inclusive vs Half-Board vs Apartment

**Against half-board:** All-inclusive typically adds €15–30 per person per night in peak season. That buys lunch, snacks and drinks. It pays back only if you stay at the resort during the day.

**Against an apartment:** Rabac has many private apartments. A self-catering couple spends about €50–80 per person per night, counting food, drinks and a few restaurant dinners. All-inclusive in July costs more than that, but not drastically for a family with children.

Rabac restaurants charge normal Istrian coastal prices. Expect around €12–16 for a pizza or pasta and €18–28 for fish dishes. Four people eating out twice a day add up quickly, which is where all-inclusive gains ground.

## Who All-Inclusive Suits in Rabac

**Families with small children.** This is the strongest case. Meals are at fixed times with child-friendly food, there are pools and kids' clubs on site, and no one needs to cook. Bellevue and the Girandella family hotels are designed for this.

**Short stays of 3–5 nights.** No shopping, no planning, and the cost is predictable. A weekend or a long-weekend break in May, June or September is the best value.

**Guests who like a drink with meals.** Local beer and wine included in the plan can cut costs for couples and groups.

## Who Is Better Off Self-Catering

- **Stays of 7+ days.** Eating at the same buffet for a week gets tiresome.
- **Active travellers.** Hiking, cycling and day trips to Plomin, Labin and Opatija mean skipping paid-for lunches.
- **Couples who want local food.** Rabac's konobas serve Istrian pasta, truffle dishes and fresh fish.
- **Small budgets in peak season.** An apartment with a market shop is the cheapest route.

The all-inclusive wristband sounds like a bargain, but in Rabac the real value is in the pool and kids' club hours. If your family spends days on the pebble beaches or on boat trips, you pay for buffets you never use. Half board is the better compromise for most couples.

## Insider Tips

- Book early. Valamar prices rise noticeably as summer approaches, and early-booking discounts are common.
- Choose May, June or September. Sea temperatures are comfortable, buffets are less crowded and rates fall by roughly 30–40% from August.
- Rabac's main beach is pebble, and the Girandella and Bellevue areas have more shade and facilities than the central town beach.
- The path along the coast links the hotels to the centre in 10–20 minutes on foot. Bellevue is uphill from the sea, so factor in the walk with a pushchair.
- Compare room-only plus Rabac's restaurants with the all-inclusive rate for your exact dates before booking.

faq.question: Is there an all-inclusive hotel in Rabac?
faq.answer: Yes. Valamar Bellevue Resort and the Girandella family hotels sell all-inclusive, and Sunny Rabac by Valamar offers a full-board plan. Other Rabac hotels mostly sell breakfast or half board.

faq.question: How much does all-inclusive cost per person in Rabac?
faq.answer: Roughly €90–170 per person per night in July and August, depending on the hotel. In May, June and September expect about €55–110. Children's discounts can lower the family total considerably.

faq.question: Is all-inclusive cheaper than half-board in Rabac?
faq.answer: No. It typically costs €15–30 more per person per night. It pays off for families who eat lunch and snacks at the hotel and for guests who drink with meals.

faq.question: Is all-inclusive better than an apartment in Rabac?
faq.answer: For families with small children and for short stays, usually yes. For stays of a week or longer, or for travellers who eat out and do day trips, an apartment is cheaper and more flexible.

faq.question: When is the best time for all-inclusive in Rabac?
faq.answer: Late May, June and September give the best balance of warm weather and lower prices. July and August have the highest rates and the busiest pools and buffets.
